description.narrative: Across Africa especially in Uganda women especially those from rural, and marginalized communities are central to food systems, natural resource management, and household energy use. Yet their voices remain largely excluded from national decision-making on agroecology, energy transitions, and climate policy. As countries pursue energy and economic transitions, there is a growing risk that policies will reinforce inequality if gender justice, care work, and grassroots realities are not centered. WoGEMUganda has been working closely with the communities that are directly affected by East Africa Crude Oil pipeline (EACOP) under Feminist Influencing basket project. This project enabled communities to create space for exchange learning, reimagining our Influencing Power, provide a practical entry point as an approach to work with communities, Government and strengthen our advocacy in agroecology and challenge false narratives in Just Energy Transition at National level. This initiative seeks to strengthenmarginalized women’s collective power, leadership, and advocacy to influence national agroecology and energy just transition policies through feminist, locally led approaches.
